source_free_concept.meaning: Lovecraftian horror means human inquiry confronting an ancient indifferent reality that makes human categories and scale inadequate. It does not require a named monster or a fixed icon.
source_free_concept.reference_scope: face and hair appearance guidance only; no identity claim, no wardrobe/body/composition lock

concepts.concept: A conservator examines a recovered glass negative in a dark photographic archive; its silver image resolves into a colossal nonhuman built surface, and an ordinary shoreline fragment reveals how little of the whole the camera recorded.
concepts.photographic_force: The fragile plate held near her attentive face places human knowledge physically against evidence whose extent exceeds the frame.
concepts.risk: A tiny inset can read as illustration; let the plate dominate enough of the frame for the alien structure to read.

concepts.concept: A cataloguer lifts a thin paper rubbing from a fossil tablet in a museum reserve; the revealed fossil contains regular architectural voids continuous with the stone growth, making a supposed specimen look like a surviving fragment of an incomprehensibly old built organism.
concepts.photographic_force: The lifted sheet is a visible before-and-after boundary; her interrupted task gives the discovery an immediate human scale.
concepts.risk: Pure carving can look like an ordinary archaeological relief; continuous mineral growth must carry the impossible implication.

concepts.concept: A woman opens one shallow archival drawer and finds its specimen bed continuing down into an immense mineral excavation beneath the cabinet; repeated drawer-scale cavities recede into a dark structure older and larger than the room.
concepts.photographic_force: A familiar hand-to-drawer relation ends at a sharply visible rupture in human scale and containment.
concepts.risk: The opening may read as a generic portal; keep continuous stone specimen strata and catalog furniture visible in the same physical view.

source_free_concept.ownership: All media, props, archival role, poses, locations, materials, lights and camera choices here are agent-owned staging, not requester requirements.
